No production source or runtime/gate implementation changes; no merge/adoption. ## Question answered

After #6778 completed the original frozen 56-call evaluation, could its poor A performance be caused by unused, swapped, reinitialized or disabled trained adapters?

## Actual read-only findings

Both original 32-update candidates contain 112 FP32 LoRA tensors across 28 q_proj/v_proj layers, totaling 544,768 parameters. Standard-library safetensors byte inspection independently reconstructs the trainer's exact registered-name parameter hash. Each candidate hash matches its frozen post-training state and the real A cold-loader receipt; all 112 tensors per arm differ from P. All 12 A output records per arm bind the same actual loaded manifest and effective policy.

Static source review traces the same trained/saved adapter through Predictor, PEFT from_pretrained and predictor.model.generate. The default adapter is active, disable_adapters starts false, and vanilla LoRA contributes B(A(x))*2. Saved inference_mode=true freezes gradients; it does not disable that contribution. Training calls train(), inference calls eval(), and both Qwen attention and LoRA dropout are zero.

No concrete implementation bug was found in this path. No torch/PEFT/transformers import, model instantiation, forward, generation, training, or native test occurred in the new readback. The main actual owner exited 0 in 0.268 seconds.

## Evidence and limits

Eight new evidence/report files include per-tensor hashes, exact source excerpts with file hashes, actual command/terminal receipts, and a plain-language readout. All new blobs match local Git identities and are below the unchanged 512,000-byte limit. Comparison against ef096991 contains exactly eight additions and no modifications or deletions.

Current installed-library source excerpts are not a historical per-token active-adapter trace; that evidence limit is explicit. The original #6778 commit/ref, all 56 raw calls, weights, budgets, old results, and NoUpdate remain unchanged. This is an evidence-only child PR, with no production/runtime/gate changes and no new learning candidate.
